newsitem.title: USA: House leaders close ranks behind Gingrich.
newsitem.headline: House leaders close ranks behind Gingrich.

text.p: House Republican leaders closed ranks behind Newt Gingrich Tuesday following suggestions by some Republicans that he step aside as House Speaker until ethics questions were resolved.

The leaders, including all of Gingrich's top lieutenants, gave the speaker much of the credit for retaining a Republican majority in the House and declared: "We unequivocally support Newt's re-election as speaker for the 105th Congress."

Representative Chris Shays of Connecticut has said he could not vote for Gingrich as speaker unless the ethics issue is settled. He said he would vote for Gingrich as the Republican nominee for speaker but, if the issue remained unsettled, would abstain when the nomination goes before the new House in January.

Representative Steve Largent of Oklahoma said in a weekend television interview that he would favour veteran Representative Henry Hyde of Illinois taking over as speaker while Gingrich dealt with the charges. He said he thought there would be some support among other House Republicans for such a move.

Hailing the Republicans' first re-election as House majority party in 68 years, a statement issued by the 15 Republicans said: "It took an entire team to win this historic victory, but no one deserves more credit than our speaker, Newt Gingrich."
It said Gingrich had visited 134 congressional districts to support incumbents and candidates over the past two years, raising millions of dollars in campaign contributions.
The House Ethics Committee is investigating charges that a tax-exempt foundation formerly headed by Gingrich used money illegally for political purposes.

In September the committee expanded its inquiries to include four additional areas, including whether Gingrich had "provided accurate, reliable and complete information" about a college course that he taught.

Referring to the investigation, the Republican statement charged that "the Democrats have carried out a political assault against the speaker, seeking to damage him through abuse of the ethics process."
